$$0\to A_\bullet\to B_\bullet\to C_\bullet\to0$$
that is exact in each degree as a sequence in the ambient abelian category.

Let $C_\bullet$ be a chain complex in an abelian category and fix $n\in\mathbb
Z$.

The **$n$th cycle subobject** of $C$ is
$$Z_n(C):=\ker(d_n)\hookrightarrow C_n.$$

The **$n$th boundary subobject** of $C$ is
$$B_n(C):=\operatorname{im}(d_{n+1})\hookrightarrow C_n.$$

Thus both are subobjects of $C_n$, one defined by the kernel of $d_n$ and the
other by the image of $d_{n+1}$.

Given a morphism of short exact sequences in an abelian category

```tikzcd
0 \arrow[r] & A \arrow[r, "i"] \arrow[d, "a"'] & B \arrow[r, "p"] \arrow[d, "b"'] & C \arrow[r] \arrow[d, "c"'] & 0 \\
0 \arrow[r] & A' \arrow[r, "i'"'] & B' \arrow[r, "p'"'] & C' \arrow[r] & 0,
```

the induced kernel sequence
$$0 \to \ker(a) \to \ker(b) \to \ker(c)$$

$$\operatorname{coker}(a) \to \operatorname{coker}(b) \to \operatorname{coker}(c) \to 0$$
is exact at $\operatorname{coker}(b)$ and at $\operatorname{coker}(c)$.
